articles.title: Hitobito OAuth tokens inherit the full role set of their user
articles.excerpt: Hitobito OAuth tokens inherit the full role set of their user Hitobito manages hierarchical groups, members, roles and events. Its access model is derived from the roles a person holds in different gr…
articles.body: Hitobito OAuth tokens inherit the full role set of their user Hitobito manages hierarchical groups, members, roles and events. Its access model is derived from the roles a person holds in different groups, which makes the API and OAuth token scope an extension of that model rather than a separate permission universe. The project's JSON API documentation states that personal OAuth access tokens have the same permissions as the corresponding user. It also says the relevant people must have a role in the defined permission range. That is a useful property for integrations and a dangerous one for long-lived tokens created by administrators or power users.

articles.body: 들어가며 예치금을 다루는 시스템에서 금액의 오차는 작더라도 그냥 넘길 수 없습니다. 그런데 금액이 틀렸다는 사실을 아는 것과, 왜 틀렸는지를 아는 것은 전혀 다른 문제였습니다. 이번 글에서는 하루치 합계를 비교하던 예치금 정합성 배치를, 주문 1건의 기대값에서 출발하는 구조로 바꾼 과정을 이야기합니다. 기존 구조: 하루치 합계를 비교하는 양식 예치금의 정합성을 보여주는 템플릿이 있습니다. 핵심은 다음 한 줄로 정리됩니다. 오늘자 거래 집계 금액 = 오늘과 어제 사이의 거래금액 차이 결제금액, 수수료 등 여러 항목의 하루치 데이터를 집계하고, 그 합을 비교해 오차를 확인하는 방식이었습니다. 문제: 오차는 보이는데 원인은 보이지 않는다 이 구조에는 두 가지 문제가 있었습니다. 1. 계산이 오래 걸렸습니다 하루치 거래금액, 즉 오늘까지의 거래금액과 어제까지의 거래금액의 차이를 각각 계산하기 위해 DB 전체를 뒤져야 했습니다. 2. 오차의 원인을 추적하기 어려웠습니다 오늘자 거래 합계만으로는 어떤 주문에 문제가 있는지 알 수 없었습니다. 주문 1건이 잘못된 것인지 여러 건이 잘못되어 그 합으로 오차가 발생한 것인지 서로 다른 항목의 이슈가 상쇄되어 드러나지 않은 것은 없는지 합계는 이상 여부를 확인하는 데는 유용합니다. 하지만 합산 과정에서 건별 정보가 사라지기 때문에, 원인을 찾는 데는 도움이 되지 않았습니다. 오차 하나를 찾아내는 데 꼬박 하루가 걸리기도 했습니다. 전환점: 주문이 단 1건뿐이라면? 일단 하나씩, 거래 집계부터 풀어보기로 했습니다. 출발점은 단순한 질문이었습니다.

articles.title: Bluetooth Mesh Battery Devices: Why Can They Report Promptly but Not Receive Control Immediately?
articles.excerpt: Imagine a battery-powered door sensor: opening the door quickly produces a phone notification, but changing its settings from the phone takes a while to take effect. Why can the same device be quick t…
articles.body: Imagine a battery-powered door sensor: opening the door quickly produces a phone notification, but changing its settings from the phone takes a while to take effect. Why can the same device be quick to report, yet slower to receive? It is not necessarily poor reception or a stuck program. A Bluetooth Mesh device using low-power mechanisms may follow different schedules for transmitting and receiving. Here is the short answer: a local event can wake a device to transmit, while messages sent to it during sleep may be stored by a Friend until it requests them. Diagnose the delay by separating those paths. This article explains how devices reduce listening, how a Friend stores messages, and how to check whether energy saving affects the response your application needs.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova later caleld the Tycho supernova with his bare eyes. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago.

articles.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
articles.excerpt: Spotted a dazzling light in the eastern sky before sunrise? It's Venus, and the planet is only going to get brighter as it heads toward its spectacular peak later this month.
articles.body: Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky.

articles.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
articles.excerpt: Company said a "multifront cyberattack" included AI agents and an on-path data snatch.
articles.body: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information—including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens—for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public sources have revealed a long list of high-profile customers, including government agencies such as the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, and the US Air Force, as well as private companies such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It's unclear if the data theft exposed customers to additional threats. We regret to inform you...

articles.body: I have been waiting to get my hands on a pair of Unistellar Envision smart binoculars since they were announced in 2024. Our editor-in-chief tried an early demo of them last year and said that they felt like something out of Star Trek . He was, of course, referencing the red augmented reality (AR) overlay in the Envisions that can identify night sky targets and landmarks, as well as displaying navigational tools. These are the first pair of smart binoculars that can identify targets in the night sky, such as planets, stars and deep space objects. The build is solid and while they aren't the most lightweight binoculars , the body is hiding that extra technology that enables the AR overlay in the right hand lens.

articles.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
articles.excerpt: The Andromeda galaxy is one of the most distant things you can see with the naked eye. The difficult part isn't finding it. It's believing that faint smudge really is another galaxy.
articles.body: The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened.
